It was declared at SoC level but mostly used to pass mainboard data from mainboard code to itself and FSP data from FSP code to itself. Now that no board/ SoC code uses it anymore, we can finally drop it. BACKPORT: mm, shmem: add internal shmem resident memory accounting Currently looking at /proc/<pid>/status or statm, there is no way to distinguish shmem pages from pages mapped to a regular file (shmem pages are mapped to /dev/zero), even though their implication in actual memory use is quite different. The internal accounting currently counts shmem pages together with regular files. As a preparation to extend the userspace interfaces, this patch adds MM_SHMEMPAGES counter to mm_rss_stat to account for shmem pages separately from MM_FILEPAGES. The next patch will expose it to userspace - this patch doesn't change the exported values yet, by adding up MM_SHMEMPAGES to MM_FILEPAGES at places where MM_FILEPAGES was used before. The only user-visible change after this patch is the OOM killer message that separates the reported "shmem-rss" from "file-rss". BACKPORT: mm, procfs: breakdown RSS for anon, shmem and file in /proc/pid/status There are several shortcomings with the accounting of shared memory (SysV shm, shared anonymous mapping, mapping of a tmpfs file). The values in /proc/<pid>/status and <...>/statm don't allow to distinguish between shmem memory and a shared mapping to a regular file, even though theirs implication on memory usage are quite different: during reclaim, file mapping can be dropped or written back on disk, while shmem needs a place in swap. Also, to distinguish the memory occupied by anonymous and file mappings, one has to read the /proc/pid/statm file, which has a field for the file mappings (again, including shmem) and total memory occupied by these mappings (i.e. equivalent to VmRSS in the <...>/status file. Getting the value for anonymous mappings only is thus not exactly user-friendly (the statm file is intended to be rather efficiently machine-readable). To address both of these shortcomings, this patch adds a breakdown of VmRSS in /proc/<pid>/status via new fields RssAnon, RssFile and RssShmem, making use of the previous preparatory patch. These fields tell the user the memory occupied by private anonymous pages, mapped regular files and shmem, respectively. Other existing fields in /status and /statm files are left without change. The /statm file can be extended in the future, if there's a need for that. Example (part of) /proc/pid/status output including the new Rss* fields: VmPeak: 2001008 kB VmSize: 2001004 kB VmLck: 0 kB VmPin: 0 kB VmHWM: 5108 kB VmRSS: 5108 kB RssAnon: 92 kB RssFile: 1324 kB RssShmem: 3692 kB VmData: 192 kB VmStk: 136 kB VmExe: 4 kB VmLib: 1784 kB VmPTE: 3928 kB VmPMD: 20 kB VmSwap: 0 kB HugetlbPages: 0 kB BUG=chromium:957990 TEST=build/boot hana, cat /proc/<pid>/status and look for above Rss* fields [vbabka@suse.cz: forward-porting, tweak changelog] Signed-off-by: Jerome Marchand <jmarchan@redhat.com> Signed-off-by: Vlastimil Babka <vbabka@suse.cz> Acked-by: Konstantin Khlebnikov <khlebnikov@yandex-team.ru> Acked-by: Michal Hocko <mhocko@suse.com> Acked-by: Hugh Dickins <hughd@google.com> Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org> Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org> (cherry picked from commit 8cee852ec53fb530f10ccabf1596734209ae336b) Signed-off-by: Sonny Rao <sonnyrao@chromium.org> [SR: 3.18: trivial context conflict] Conflicts: fs/proc/task_mmu.c Change-Id: I1561fe4064a5983823a3094e649d3e9b55d6e3c8 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1600739 Commit-Ready: Sonny Rao <sonnyrao@chromium.org> Tested-by: Sonny Rao <sonnyrao@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Luigi Semenzato <semenzato@chromium.org>

power: Manipulate wake mask during s0ix timeouts When S0ix failure detection is enabled and a timeout occurs such that the SLP_S0 line never actually toggles, then s0ix_transition_timeout() sets the HANG_DETECT event bit. This doesn't quite work in this scenario, since the wake mask is only enabled when the power state transitions to S0ix, which happens when the SLP_S0 line toggles. So the AP never sees the event, since it's not in the wake mask and so never causes the EC->AP interrupt line to change. Detect this situation in the timeout function, and explicitly move the wake mask to its S0ix value so that when the event bit is set, (if it is in the wake mask), the system will wake up. Doing this forcefully gets the wake mask out of sync with the power state. So upon resume, explicitly restore the wake mask to its S0 state. hostap_config: re-enforce HT requirements Pure N should require HT support. We don't want to continue handicapping ourselves for daisy/snow. (Or at least, we shouldn't keep whining about this condition.) It happens that all supported devices now work fine with require_ht, so let's turn it back on. Per hostapd, "require_ht" and "require_vht" mean including the HT or VHT BSS selector in the Supported rates (or Extended supported rates) IE, which means that the client station must support HT or VHT in order to associate. It does *not* mean that the AP won't also advertise legacy (non-(V)HT) rates, and so clients are still allowed to regress from HT to legacy rates. Given the above, it's not 100% clear how we should translate 11xx_PURE into hostapd properties. Particularly, 11AC_PURE could be interpreted to mean: * require VHT or * require HT and VHT I've selected the former for now, as it's the least churn, but we can update this choice later if desired. CHROMIUM: Bluetooth: Fix broken ble re-advertisement feature BLE advertisment needs to be re-enabled in kernel when previous ble connection goes away. This feature is broken from the commit 5084500d59bb ("CHROMIUM: Bluetooth: Remove the assumption on the Adv state in connection event") in 11/2017, this feature is broken in cros kernel 3.10, 3.14, 3.18 and 4.4. I have verified this feature using several linux kernels, including 4.19.25 in raspi 3 + ble dongle, and confirm ble advertisment needs to be re-enabled in __hci_req_schedule_adv_instance from kernel bluetooth when previous BLE connection goes away. Confirm with Luiz Augusto von Denz from bluetooth upstream, BLE advertisement needs to be re-enabled by kernel when previous BLE connection goes away, this feature has been there in bluetooth kernel upstream for several years. The code logic is roughly as below. When BLE connection is established, HCI_LE_ADV flag needs to be cleared via hci_dev_clear_flag(hdev, HCI_LE_ADV) in hci_le_conn_complete_evt, Linux bluetooth use this flag to check if advertisment is there. a. When there is no ble connection and ble advertisment is there, __hci_req_schedule_adv_instance is peridically called, and if that is just rescheduling the same instance, it does not execute any HCI command, and return since HCI_LE_ADV has been set, and it use same adv instance. b. When ble connection is established, HCI_LE_ADV flag is cleared in hci_le_conn_complete_evt. Then __hci_req_schedule_adv_instance would be periodically called, and it would goes to __hci_req_enable_advertising and does not enable advertisement since connection is there. c. When ble disconnection happens, when __hci_req_schedule_adv_instance is called again, it found HCI_LE_ADV has been cleared in b, and goes to call __hci_req_enable_advertising, and found ble connection is not there, and re-enable ble advertisement. Regarding the chromium:776423, it seems the previous fix is not right, it should be addressed by the below ways a.by the controller, fix Connection Failed to be Established issues. b.in kernel side, from hci_cs_le_read_remote_features() of hci_event.c, when the return status is not successful, setting LE advertising flag to true if it is cleared in hci_le_conn_complete_evt() previously in a connection attempt. c.Add "LE Set Advertise Enable" command with 0x00 (disabled) before the next "LE Set Advertising Parameters" command when hitting the error on LE read remote used features command. Either way, it should not break the ble re-advertisment feature. Revert "CHROMIUM: Bluetooth: Remove the assumption on the Adv state in connection event" This reverts commit 5084500d59bb4e09b01d5323323b2cf7e0758611. CHROMIUM: Bluetooth: Fix broken ble re-advertisement feature BLE advertisment needs to be re-enabled in kernel when previous ble connection goes away. This feature is broken from the commit 5084500d59bb ("CHROMIUM: Bluetooth: Remove the assumption on the Adv state in connection event") in 11/2017, this feature is broken in cros kernel 3.10, 3.14, 3.18 and 4.4. I have verified this feature using several linux kernels, including 4.19.25 in raspi 3 + ble dongle, and confirm ble advertisment needs to be re-enabled in __hci_req_schedule_adv_instance from kernel bluetooth when previous BLE connection goes away. Confirm with Luiz Augusto von Denz from bluetooth upstream, BLE advertisement needs to be re-enabled by kernel when previous BLE connection goes away, this feature has been there in bluetooth kernel upstream for several years. The code logic is roughly as below. When BLE connection is established, HCI_LE_ADV flag needs to be cleared via hci_dev_clear_flag(hdev, HCI_LE_ADV) in hci_le_conn_complete_evt, Linux bluetooth use this flag to check if advertisment is there. a. When there is no ble connection and ble advertisment is there, __hci_req_schedule_adv_instance is peridically called, and if that is just rescheduling the same instance, it does not execute any HCI command, and return since HCI_LE_ADV has been set, and it use same adv instance. b. When ble connection is established, HCI_LE_ADV flag is cleared in hci_le_conn_complete_evt. Then __hci_req_schedule_adv_instance would be periodically called, and it would goes to __hci_req_enable_advertising and does not enable advertisement since connection is there. c. When ble disconnection happens, when __hci_req_schedule_adv_instance is called again, it found HCI_LE_ADV has been cleared in b, and goes to call __hci_req_enable_advertising, and found ble connection is not there, and re-enable ble advertisement. Regarding the chromium:776423, it seems the previous fix is not right, it should be addressed by the below ways a.by the controller, fix Connection Failed to be Established issues. b.in kernel side, from hci_cs_le_read_remote_features() of hci_event.c, when the return status is not successful, setting LE advertising flag to true if it is cleared in hci_le_conn_complete_evt() previously in a connection attempt. c.Add "LE Set Advertise Enable" command with 0x00 (disabled) before the next "LE Set Advertising Parameters" command when hitting the error on LE read remote used features command. Either way, it should not break the ble re-advertisment feature. Revert "CHROMIUM: Bluetooth: Remove the assumption on the Adv state in connection event" This reverts commit 5084500d59bb4e09b01d5323323b2cf7e0758611. CHROMIUM: cros_ec: use ODR events to clear the spreading history This uses the ODR flag introduced in CL:1450288 to clear the last batch data used by the spreading algorithm. The spreading code relies on accurately measuring the effective interval between batches of samples. An ODR change means that the previous batches may no longer represent the behavior of the EC. If an ODR change is immediately followed by a batch, the AP will attempt to spread based on the previous interval, which can easily lead to "spreading into the future", leading to subsequent timestamp mismatch errors. This patch solves that problem by having ODR events be breaking points for the spreading code. The tradeoff is that this can cause samples to be lost immediately after an ODR change. This problem can't effectively be solved without either: - storing those samples in a side queue and spreading them once updated information becomes available to do so; - communicating the ODR to the AP as part of the ODR event. Notes: 1) do not use ODR change and FLUSH events as input to the filter; these events come asynchronously to the regular flow of data, and including them in the filter history as the potential to disrupt the slope calculation; 2) clear the previous batch as well as the current on an ODR change; it is theoretically possible for us to reopen an old batch after an ODR change which would not work for the same reason reopening the current batch would not work.
